target: SWE intern / new-grad roles (general software engineering, 2026–27 recruiting cycle)
seven_second_takeaway: UMD CS '28; AWS and Capital One SWE internships plus an Amazon contract role; heavy AWS serverless work; a C++ IEX order-book project; co-founded a 110-member campus studio.

score_rationale.impact_clarity: Several bullets end on a tech list (Kinesis/Lambda/API Gateway, X-Ray/SNS) instead of an outcome; the AWS and IEX bullets describe activity without results.
score_rationale.quantification: The 34%, 65% and 90% figures have no stated metric or baseline. The IEX benchmarks were measured but no numbers are reported, which is the worst miss for a systems reader.
score_rationale.technical_depth: IEX and Capital One search-index bullets show real design choices; Amazon contract bullets lean toward AWS service enumeration over decisions.
score_rationale.concision_readability: Most bullets run a full two lines; tech chains like 'Docker + AWS Fargate via GitHub Actions, with AWS CDK (TypeScript)' slow the read.
score_rationale.credibility: Four roles run concurrently (AWS Redmond overlapping College Park contract, UMIACS, TerpLabs). Satisfaction percentages with unclear sample sizes invite skepticism.
score_rationale.domain_fit: Strong for general SWE, but the AWS intern role, the biggest brand, has the weakest bullet, and backend wins are buried under service names.

must_fix: Clarify: the IEX project says throughput/latency were measured with rdtscp and perf but reports no result. State what the LSM vs B+ tree comparison found, or reframe the bullet so it doesn't promise a number.
Clarify: what the 34% speedup measures (end-to-end latency? throughput?) and what the 65% baseline was. Unlabeled percentages fall apart under one follow-up question.

Clarify the overlapping dates: an AWS Redmond internship (Sep–Dec 2026) running alongside 'Present' roles in College Park reads as a conflict. Mark the concurrent ones part-time/remote or end-date them.
Clarify: '90% satisfaction' and '93% meal satisfaction' need a scope (how many users/testers) or should be softened; otherwise they read as survey filler.

bullets.quote: Researching and implementing Java-based utilization optimizations for
bullets.issue: Your biggest brand gets one vague bullet; 'utilization' of what? No component, technique or status.
bullets.suggestion: Name the Redshift subsystem and the kind of optimization (if disclosable); 'Researching and implementing' can stay since it's ongoing, but say what is being optimized.

bullets.quote: Rebuilt the legacy UI of a test-data workflow
bullets.issue: Three frameworks in the lead clause; '90% satisfaction vs. the old tool' has no scope or survey basis.
bullets.suggestion: Rebuilt a legacy test-data workflow builder in React/Electron with a React-Flow editor and Jest-tested validation; users rated it 90% satisfaction vs. the old tool (clarify sample).

bullets.quote: Built a precomputed tree-style workflow search index to
bullets.issue: Good design choice, but the 'why' (access limits) and outcome are buried; 'distilling popular workflows' is unclear.
bullets.suggestion: To work within DB access limits, built a precomputed tree-structured search index over popular workflows from a 270K+ row PostgreSQL table (Python/SQLAlchemy, Redis), minimizing live DB queries.

bullets.quote: Cut workflow generation time 65% to under 15s
bullets.issue: Strong result; 'Claude skill using sub-skill decomposition' is jargon a general HM may not parse.
bullets.suggestion: Cut workflow generation time 65% to under 15s by decomposing an LLM agent (Claude) into sub-tasks with Python search/validation tools, guided by CloudWatch + OpenSearch latency logs.

bullets.quote: Shipped an Amazon Leo space-research tool adopted into
bullets.issue: 'Adopted into Leo's ecosystem' is the win but vague; the deploy-stack chain dominates the line.
bullets.suggestion: Shipped a space-research tool adopted into Amazon Leo's internal ecosystem; containerized on Fargate with CI/CD (GitHub Actions) and CDK infra-as-code so new engineers can onboard.

bullets.quote: Sped up a pipeline routing 6,000+ scraped research
bullets.issue: 34% of what metric? Bullet ends on a service list instead of the design decision.
bullets.suggestion: Cut [latency/throughput — clarify] 34% on a pipeline routing 6,000+ scraped research docs to inference by moving to Kinesis streams feeding Lambda processors, served via API Gateway.

bullets.quote: Automated fine-tuning of an AWS Bedrock source-relevancy model
bullets.issue: Decision gates skipping redundant retraining is the interesting part; lead with it, drop the service roll call.
bullets.suggestion: Automated retraining of a Bedrock source-relevancy model on EventBridge schedules, with decision gates that skip redundant runs; added X-Ray tracing and SNS failure alerts.

bullets.quote: Developing automated training for PhysTwin, a physics-based
bullets.issue: 'Automated training' of what, and what does your piece do? Venue target is the only concrete detail.
bullets.suggestion: Clarify what was automated (parameter fitting? data pipeline?) and your specific contribution, keeping the ICLR-target context.

bullets.quote: Engineered a Python pipeline rendering AnyGrasp multi-camera grasp
Reduced research-environment setup time 30% with uv
bullets.issue: Two separate ideas: setup time win and profiling/tests; the profiling clause has no result.
bullets.suggestion: Cut research-environment setup time 30% via uv dependency pinning and Docker; added psutil time/memory profiling and Pytest suites to locate bottlenecks.

bullets.quote: Co-founded and scaled a 110+ member campus product

bullets.suggestion: Built the data layer for Tortuga, a class scheduler with 20,000+ visits in its first 30 days, using Prisma SQL queries with Redis caching to reduce DB load and latency.

bullets.quote: Building a RAG meal-suggestion feature for the official
